name: compose-luma-with-the-residual-branch-disabled
rationale:
composeLuma is the luma half of a Dolby Vision composer: each thread reads four base-layer texels, looks each one up in a polynomial table, optionally adds a non-linear-quantized residual decoded from four enhancement-layer texels, then offsets, arithmetic-shifts, clamps and narrows the four results back to ushort in one vector. The three uncovered symbols are the two ends of that narrowing -- `air.convert.s.v4i32.u.v4i16` widening the enhancement layer and `air.convert.u.v4i16.s.v4i32` narrowing the answer -- and `air.sign.v4f32`, which is what makes the residual decode odd-symmetric around its offset.

The residual is `sign(d)` folded into an affine map of `d = el - nlq_offset`: it forms `u = 4*(2d - sign(d))`, scales by SL and adds `sign(d)*T`, clamps to +/- RR, multiplies by nlq_rshift and subtracts one more when `u` is negative, and finally forces the whole thing to zero when `d` is exactly zero. Three of those four steps read the sign, so a lowering that returned the wrong sign at any argument would move the answer by tens. The eight enhancement values run 0 through 7 against an offset of 4, which puts one lane on each side of the discontinuity and one lane exactly on it, and RR = 12 makes the clamp bite at three of the eight.

Every intermediate is an exact small integer in binary32 -- the offset, T and RR are integers, SL is a half and the doubling and quadrupling are exact -- so the float-to-int truncation that ends the residual never has to choose between two integers, and the fast-math flags cannot move it. The shift is arithmetic rather than logical, and the smallest sum here is negative, so a logical shift would turn -17 into a number above two billion instead of -9, and the lower clamp would report 300 rather than 0.

The base-layer values run 0 through 7 and the polynomial table is eight entries a hundred apart, so each of the eight table slots is named by a different output; a wrong table index shows up as a whole hundred. The four lanes of each thread carry different base and enhancement values, so a lowering that broadcast one lane over the vector would disagree at every thread.

This case sets `disable_residual_flag`, which is the arm where the enhancement layer is never read at all and the residual is a constant zero. It runs the same base-layer lookup, offset, shift, clamp and narrowing over the same inputs, so the difference between the two cases is exactly the residual -- and with the residual gone, the smallest sum is no longer negative, so the arithmetic shift and the lower clamp go quiet and only the upper clamp is left.

name: copy-every-cube-face-through-its-own-width
rationale: The kernel reconstructs a cube direction from the grid position and the width the texture reports, so a wrong width moves the sample off the texel centre. A 2x2 face is the smallest size at which that shows: the reconstructed face coordinate is (gid + 0.5) / width, which is a texel centre only when width is two, and the nearest-filter sampler then returns that exact texel rather than a neighbour. All 96 lanes are k/128 for k from 1 to 96, every one an exact half and all distinct, so the result is the identity on the whole cube and any permutation of the six faces, any transposed or flipped face axis, and any off-by-one texel are each visible. The mapping the answer pins is that face f texel (x, y) becomes array slice f texel (x, y), with no axis flip on either side.

name: load-and-store-through-a-pointer-chosen-at-runtime
rationale: Three things you can do with a pointer chosen at runtime, none of which had an authored case. Logical SPIR-V cannot merge pointers into two different descriptors into one value, so each has to be replayed in the value domain. Loading through a cross-buffer selected pointer is emit_selected_pointer_direct_load / emit_selected_direct_load_arm_value / selected_direct_load_arm_pointer (10 corpus sources each, 0 cased). Storing through one is emit_selected_pointer_direct_store, which NO corpus source reaches at all. Selecting a BASE and then indexing it is emit_selected_pointer_gep / emit_selected_pointer_access_chain / emit_selected_pointer_load (59, 53 and 50 sources, 1 cased each). The same-buffer store-target select also drives emit_raw_pointer_select_index. a = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128) and b = (1000 .. 8000), all exact binary32 and disjoint in magnitude so any arm confusion is unmistakable. Lanes 0-3 take the a arm and lanes 4-7 the b arm for the load, and the store target select sends the low lanes to out[gid] and the high ones to out[gid+8], so out[4..11] must come back UNTOUCHED at its 0xAB initial pattern -- a store through the wrong arm lands exactly there. The base select is deliberately inverted relative to the load select (b for the low lanes), so a case that confused the two would answer with a's values in both halves. The AIR is hand-written because no Metal source reliably produces a cross-descriptor pointer select the frontend does not flatten first.

name: compact-eight-visible-particles-into-a-claimed-run
rationale:
Covers air.simd_prefix_exclusive_sum.s.i8, air.simd_sum.s.i8 and air.simd_broadcast_first.s.i32, and exercises the threadgroup-scoped air.simdgroup.barrier this shader spells around them, together with air.simd_is_first and air.atomic.global.add.s.i32.

Both cull switches in the uniforms are off -- cullFullyTransparent at byte 101 and cullOutsideFrustum at byte 100 -- which makes every particle visible without reading a frustum plane, a particle position or a size, and leaves the compaction as the only live work. That is also why the four function constants are declared false and do not matter: their regions sit behind cullFullyTransparent.

Loop bound: the only loop walks the six frustum planes and exits at index 6. With cullOutsideFrustum off the entry branches around it entirely, so the authored dispatch runs no iterations at all.

The header's first description points at offset 0 of the data buffer, where the particle count is 8, so all eight threads of the single threadgroup pass the count test and all eight lanes stay active through the simd reduction. The exclusive prefix sum of one per lane is the lane's rank, the sum is eight, and the first lane claims a run of eight from the visible counter. That counter starts at 5 rather than 0, so the claimed base is 5 and it has to survive the broadcast: the run lands at visible[5..13] and the surrounding poison bytes stay poison. A lowering that broadcast the wrong lane, ranked the lanes in another order, or counted inactive lanes moves the run or its contents. Expected output is 20 poison bytes, the ints 0 through 7, then 12 poison bytes.

name: round-half-away-from-zero-image-scale
rationale: imageScale computes round(input.r * scale) and clamps it to [0, 255]. The scale buffer is 1.0 and the four read-only texels are 2.5, 0.5, 1.5 and 3.5, so every lane feeds air.fast_round.f32 an exact .5 tie. Metal breaks those ties away from zero and answers 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0; a round-half-to-even rounding would answer 2.0, 0.0, 2.0, 4.0 in lanes 0 and 1, so the captured write-only texture distinguishes the two tie rules byte-exactly.

name: sample-each-of-three-textures-through-one-dynamic-array-index
rationale:
A dynamically indexed `metal::array` of three SAMPLED textures read through one sampler -- the half of `native/opaque_image_select.rs` that no authored case reached. Logical SPIR-V has no pointer-to-image, so the emitter cannot name the handle the index picks; it collects the whole store set into the alloca, replays it as a select tree over the three image ids, and proves every arm is available at the sample site. A sampled image is a different SPIR-V value from a directly read one (`OpSampledImage`, not `OpImage`) and needs its own image-type recovery, which is why the file has two halves. The corpus has exactly one host for this half, an 870-line tone mapper; a twenty-line fixture reaches the same rules.

Measured with per-function coverage against every cased source: 18 functions no cased source reaches, being `plan_tree`, `replay_selected_image`, `sampled_image_image_type`, `is_sampled_image_value_op`, `tree_values_available_at` and `value_available_at` with their closures, plus `collect_select_tree`, `fresh` and `tir::operands::extract_aggregate_member`.

All three arms are live in one dispatch of three threads. `which` is (2, 0, 1) rather than the identity, so a select tree wired in the wrong order answers differently instead of agreeing by accident; `% 3` keeps the index in range without letting the frontend fold it, because the value comes from a buffer.

The comparison is exact. Texture k's texel (x, y) carries the four channels 100(k+1) + 10(2y + x) + c for c in 1..4, and the shader folds them as r + 10g + 100b + 1000a. The sampler is `nearest`, `clamp_to_edge` and normalized, so (0.25, 0.75) on a 2x2 image resolves to texel (0, 1) with no filtering at all: 0.25 * 2 = 0.5 and 0.75 * 2 = 1.5 each land strictly inside their own texel, neither on a boundary, so no rounding rule is being relied on. Every term and every partial sum is an integer below 2^24, exactly representable in binary32, so the `fast` reassociation the frontend is free to apply cannot move the result. The three answers are 359841, 137641 and 248741: the texture index sets the hundred-thousands digit and the texel index sets the tens, so a wrong image and a wrong texel are separately visible, and the output buffer is pre-filled with -1.0, which no arm can produce. Metal answered exactly those three floats, derived in advance, and MoltenVK Matches.
